graph.summary: Tamoxifen → Endoxifen → Estrogen receptor alpha → cell population proliferation → Breast Cancer

evidence.snippet: Tamoxifen requires metabolic activation by cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes for formation of active metabolites, 4-hydroxytamoxifen and endoxifen, which have 30- to 100-fold greater affinity to the estrogen receptor and the potency to suppress estrogen-dependent breast cancer cell proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Tamoxifen is metabolized by CYP enzymes to its active metabolite endoxifen.

paper.title: Pharmacogenomics of tamoxifen: roles of drug metabolizing enzymes and transporters.

evidence.snippet: endoxifen blocks ERalpha transcriptional activity and inhibits estrogen-induced breast cancer cell proliferation even in the presence of tamoxifen, N-desmethyl-tamoxifen, and 4-hydroxytamoxifen.
evidence.explanation: Endoxifen is a potent antiestrogen that blocks ERalpha transcriptional activity and targets it for degradation, after binding the receptor with high affinity.

paper.title: The tamoxifen metabolite, endoxifen, is a potent antiestrogen that targets estrogen receptor alpha for degradation in breast cancer cells.

evidence.snippet: G1T48 is a potent and efficacious inhibitor of estrogen-mediated transcription and proliferation in ER-positive breast cancer cells, similar to the pure antiestrogen fulvestrant.
evidence.explanation: Estrogen receptor signaling mediates (drives) proliferation in ER-positive breast cancer cells; inhibiting ER inhibits proliferation.

paper.title: G1T48, an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader, and the CDK4/6 inhibitor lerociclib inhibit tumor growth in animal models of endocrine-resistant breast cancer.

evidence.snippet: Knockdown of FOXK2 significantly inhibited breast cancer cell proliferation, migration, anchorage-independent growth, and delayed tumor growth in a xenograft mouse model.
evidence.explanation: Breast cancer cell proliferation drives tumor growth in breast cancer.

paper.title: FOXK2 amplification promotes breast cancer development and chemoresistance.
